Plot a food web

Source: R/plot_foodweb.R
plot_foodweb.Rd

Draws the food web of a model from its diet table (see create_diet_table()): nodes are the groups (and the detritus in the sediment) placed by trophic level, edges go from prey to predator. Pathways can be highlighted with a table of links and colours.

Usage

plot_foodweb(
  x,
  highlight = NULL,
  x_position = NULL,
  focus = NULL,
  window = 730
)

Arguments

x

An Atlantis object with the biology and groups files loaded. If the system-wide biomass (outputBiomIndx.txt) is loaded, node size is the initial biomass and node colour the ratio of the final biomass (mean over the last window days) to the initial one.

highlight

A data frame of the links to highlight, with the columns prey, predator (group codes) and colour, and optionally pathway, the name of the pathway the link belongs to, shown in the legend. Links absent from the food web (e.g. proposed links) are drawn dashed.

x_position

A named vector of horizontal positions (names are group codes) that overrides the default layout, for some or all nodes.

focus

A vector of group codes. If not NULL, only these groups, the groups they interact with (their prey and predators) and the links involving them are drawn. Trophic levels are still computed from the whole food web.

window

Number of days at the end of the run used to compute the final biomass.

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

Edge width is the largest pPREY value over the stages of prey and predator. The trophic level of a group is 1 plus the mean of the trophic levels of its prey, weighted by these values (cannibalism ignored); groups without prey are at level 1. By default, pelagic groups are on the left and benthic groups (benthos, sediment bacteria and detritus, benthic primary producers) on the right, spread evenly within each trophic level.

Examples

my_model <- new_atlantis() |>
  atlantis_load_files(
    c(
      system.file("examples", "inputs", "tiny_biol.prm", package = "atlantio"),
      system.file("examples", "inputs", "tiny_groups.csv", package = "atlantio"),
      system.file("examples", "outputs", "outputBiomIndx.txt", package = "atlantio")
    )
  )
plot_foodweb(my_model)


pathways <- data.frame(
  prey = c("DIA", "GRN", "CAL", "GZS", "CHI"),
  predator = c("CAL", "CAL", "GZS", "WAE", "WAE"),
  colour = c("#1a9850", "#1a9850", "#1a9850", "#1a9850", "#d73027"),
  pathway = c(rep("Pelagic", 4), "Proposed")
)
plot_foodweb(my_model, highlight = pathways)


# Walleye, its prey and its predators only
plot_foodweb(my_model, focus = "WAE")
